content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Edward Fleming (E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes:
- HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say full_time employee, role Payroll Specialist. Recommendation: write.
- Security says contractor with basic security training. Recommendation: read.

This is a conflict. 5 notes say full_time, 1 note says contractor. The Security note says it looked up employment type in own database and found contractor, differing from HR's full_time.

Which to trust? Typically HR is the source of truth for employment type. The majority (5 notes) say full_time. The security note is a single dissenting note, and says it looked up in its own database - security may not have the employment records directly. HR database is authoritative for employment type.

Given the majority and HR being authoritative for employment type, treat Edward as full_time Payroll Specialist. For full-time employees, max is write; admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (Engineer owns it). So max is write. Requested write equals max, so grant write.

Alternatively, if contractor with basic training, max read, requested write above max, grant read.

The decision hinges on employment type. The majority of notes (5) say full_time, including HR which looked up in own database. The security note appears to be the outlier. I'll go with full_time → write.

Let me submit write.
